facts.fact: UNDP Togo's annual report for 2024 states that the digital birth registration platform it supported, in its pilot phase at the Golfe 3 town hall, simplified the registration of births and of other civil status acts, which it does not name.
UNDP Togo states that the digital birth registration platform was implemented in its pilot phase at the Golfe 3 town hall in 2024, one commune; no total of communes or offices is given.

UNDP Togo states that it supported the digitalisation of the civil status centres of the 16 communes of the Savanes region in 2024, which it says can now deliver acts in real time and have been trained to use the digital birth registration platform; it does not say they register on it, and gives no national total of communes or centres.

UNDP Togo states that it supported the development, deployment and operation of the digital birth registration platform, and that the birth tele-declaration in Golfe 3 was set up with its technical and financial support, in 2024; no domestic budget line is mentioned.

systems.country_label: plateforme numérique d'enregistrement des naissances; télédéclaration des naissances
systems.owner: developed, deployed and put into operation with UNDP support; the owner is not stated
systems.tiers: pilot phase at the Golfe 3 town hall; civil status centres of the 16 communes of the Savanes region trained to use it (2024). Also said to digitise the civil status registers. Golfe 3 declaration rate given as 11.92 in 2023 and 27.61% between April and November 2024

note: No made fact: the report does not say where the entry is made or where the record is held. The 16 Savanes communes are described as digitalised and trained, not as registering on the platform. The report also counts 14,800 people (8,880 men, 5,920 women) given a birth act, with no system named.
